correctness.rationale: Each vertex of K3 square Cn (n>=5) has the exact four-vertex open neighborhood tetrahedron F_{i,a}. Opposite-layer edge {v_{i−1,a},v_{i+1,a}} has exactly one common graph neighbor, yielding two genuine sequential elementary collapses per center (triangle/tetrahedron, then edge/triangle), for 6n steps. The surviving 6n triangles have 3n vertices and 9n edges, every edge lies in two oppositely oriented triangles, every vertex link is a single hexagon, and the complex is connected, orientable, closed, Euler characteristic zero: it is a PL torus. Thus pi1=Z² and integral cup pairing unimodular. The only graph triangles are K3 fibers, so Aut(G_n)=S3×Dn and no automorphism acts as a 3n-cycle when 3 divides n, proving noncirculant infinite subfamily. Fresh independent finite complex enumerator checked free face pairs and exact final simplices for n=5,6,7,9,12; the arbitrary-n proof is local/surface-theoretic.
